title: Tenant noise reduction and signal fidelity checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook for reducing tenant-level noise in our telemetry and improving signal fidelity for inference-related dashboards. Goal is to make per-tenant SLI/alerting actionable without being drowned in variance from low-volume tenants or sampling artifacts.

Audience:
Platform SREs, Observability engineers, product leads owning SLAs for Hosted/Dedicated, and Solutions eng when debugging customer incidents.

High-level goals (measurable):
- Reduce false-positive tenant alerts by 60% for low-traffic tenants in 90 days.
- Increase ratio of meaningful traces per incident by 2x for token-serving regressions.
- Keep trace and metrics storage cost within current budget by using adaptive sampling and guardrails.

Key definitions (how we will compute things):
- Tenant request: single top-level API call from customer org (route + auth token).
- Effective-batch-size: average batch size for requests that hit batching window; reported per-tenant and model_variant.
- KV-cache-warm-rate: fraction of requests where KV cache hit prevents model compute (per-tenant, 1m window).
- Tenant-noise-index (TNI): composite score to decide whether a tenant should be on aggressive sampling. TNI = weighted sum of (1 / requests_per_minute), variance(latency_q95) scaled, cold-cache-rate. Higher = noisier and lower signal. (Prototype formula in TODO).
- Fidelity-score: per-tenant metric mapped 0..100 derived from sampling coverage, cache-hit consistency, and trace-completeness; used to prioritize instrumentation.

Suggested SLIs/SLOs (candidate):
- API latency p95 <= 350ms for non-streaming short prompt workloads (per-tenant aggregated, only tenants > 1 req/min included in SLO reporting).
- KV cache hit-rate >= 75% for dedicated pool tenants (30d rolling).
- Prompt-replay-coverage >= 0.5% of requests for tenants with >100k requests/month (to keep some sample of exact inputs).

Tracing and sampling strategy (practical):
- Always capture full traces for 100% of requests flagged as errors (5xx or rate-limit-on-degraded-path).
- Adaptive reservoir sampling by tenant: keep a small baseline (min 1 trace/minute) for all tenants + burst budget proportional to requests/minute (capped). Prevents cold tenants from overwhelming the reservoir.
- Stratified sampling for model_variant + route + cache_status (hit/miss): ensure each (tenant, model_variant, cache_status) cell has at least N traces/day for tenants hitting threshold.
- Event-based high-fidelity capture: when perf regression spike detected by probe (see probes section) automatically switch affected tenants to high sampling for 10 minutes.
- Trace annotations: ensure spans include tags: tenant_id, tenant_tier, model_variant, batch_size, cache_status, kv_key_presence, routing_decision, sequence_len, prompt_hash (anonymized). Avoid PII: strip any prompt text from spans; keep hashes only.

Dashboard design notes (practical widgets):
- Tenant Noise Heatmap: rows=tenant cohort (by traffic bucket), cols=day, color=TNI. Click -> tenant detail panel.
- Signal Fidelity Trend: fidelity-score over time with event markers for rollouts/quantization changes.
- Sampling Budget Utilization: daily consumed vs budget per region; hover shows top tenants using budget.
- Per-tenant SLI panel: p50/p95/p99, kv-cache-hit-rate, batch-size histogram, trace-rate/sample-rate.
- Probe vs Production comparison: small multiples of synthetic probe latency vs production p95 by tenant cohort.

Investigation runbook (operator steps):
1) Alert fires (p95 deviance or TNI spike).
2) Open tenant panel -> check trace-rate and sampling coverage. If sampling < threshold, increase reservoir for 10m and request immediate traces (via ephemeral flag).
3) Inspect span breadcrumb: batch_size and cache_status anchoring. If batch_size collapsed -> look at request shape changes (prompt length/formatting).
4) Check routing_decision tag to see fallback to smaller model variant or older quantized kernel.
5) If KV cold-cache high: check warmers for tenant, recent deploys, or migration events.
6) If the issue correlates with rollout id -> roll back or toggle canary policy.
7) Annotate incident with trace ids and link to PR/ticket.

Sampling budget and cost controls:
- Global daily trace budget hard cap (configured in telemetry infra). Per-tenant soft cap set to 0.5% of global budget by default; can be raised for strategic customers.
- Auto-throttle: if query cost > threshold, reduce non-error trace sampling rate across low-priority tenants.
- Regularly prune low-value spans (no useful tags) before storage.

Probe design (to detect fidelity regressions early):
- Multi-model synthetic probes hitting: short prompt, long prompt, streaming session, kv-heavy prompt.
- Sweep probes per region every 1m; compare probe latency and distribution to per-tenant cohorts.
- If probe deviates > 2x baseline p95 then trigger high-fidelity capture for tenants mapped to that region/model_variant.

Short todo list / next steps:
- [ ] Draft TNI formula & thresholds (owner: Maya) -> JIRA INF-2142.
- [ ] Implement tenant-level reservoir sampler in telemetry agent (owner: Arjun). PR: linked above.
- [ ] Add prompt_hash tag and review PII gating (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Wire up heatmap widget in Grafana -> mock panels and API slices (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Pilot with 10 mid-size tenants for 30d and measure alert reduction.

Notes to self / rough hypotheses:
- Low-volume tenants produce wildly unstable p95 numbers; often a single outlier request shifts percentiles. We should avoid taking action on p95 when requests_per_minute < threshold.
- Cache-warmth oscillations correlate with rollout scripts that flush prefix caches aggressively; consider phased cache invalidation.
- Batching collapse often signals a client-side throttle change (new SDK) rather than server-side regression. Keep SDK versions mapped to tenants.

References / links:
- telemetry agent sampling RFC: CONFLUENCE-OBS-SAMPLING-RFC
- prompted incident example: JIRA-INC-3341 (tenant X p95 spike correlated with rollout)
- quick query snippets (SQL/Grafana) are in the linked PR above.

Open questions for discussion:
- What minimum trace-per-cell (tenant, model_variant, cache_status) is a good heuristic? 100/day? 500/day? Need cost modeling.
- Should we include a "privileged debug" flag tenants can enable for 30min that forces full traces? Security implications.
- How to fold Dedicated tenants with reserved capacity: smaller sampling needed because of cost predictability, but more fidelity expected by enterprise customers.

If this looks reasonable I'll convert the TNI formula into a table and add mock queries for each dashboard widget in the next pass.

End of doc.
